title: Polpette al Sugo
subtitle: Italian meatballs simmered in tomato sauce
excerpt: Beef and pork meatballs, seasoned with Parmesan and parsley, browned and then simmered slowly in a simple tomato sauce until tender. Serve with pasta or bread to catch every drop of the sauce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Polpette (meatballs) are eaten throughout Italy, but contrary to Italian-American restaurant practice, they are not traditionally served on top of spaghetti in Italy. In Italian cooking, polpette are most often eaten as a secondo (second course), separate from the pasta course, or served in broth. Italian-American polpette on spaghetti is an immigrant adaptation. Polpette al sugo, simmered in tomato sauce, is the classic preparation: the meatballs cook gently in the sauce, flavouring it, while the sauce keeps the meat moist and tender.

recipeTools.notes: Wide enough to hold all the meatballs in a single layer.

content.text: Use a mix of beef and pork mince if you can: the pork keeps the meatballs moist and adds fat that beef alone lacks. Soak the breadcrumbs in milk before mixing: this is the trick that gives a soft, tender texture rather than a dense one. Roll them firmly so they hold together, then brown well in batches before the sauce goes in. Once in the sauce, they cook on a very gentle simmer.

Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes until absorbed. Mix together the beef, pork, soaked breadcrumbs, Parmesan, garlic, parsley, egg, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Combine gently with your hands, then roll into balls about 3 to 4 cm in diameter. You should get around 20 meatballs.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, fry the remaining 2 garlic cloves (sliced) for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and crush roughly. Season. Bring to a simmer.

Return the meatballs to the pan. Simmer on the lowest heat, partially covered, for 30 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through and the sauce has thickened. Tear in the basil. Serve with pasta or crusty bread.
